checks.check: Mailing destination reviewed before filing a change of address
checks.why: Choose a mailing address you can use. USPS licenses permanent change-of-address data; its full-service dataset covers 48 months.

checks.check: Private mailing address used where accepted
checks.why: Keep required residence and identity addresses accurate. Banks generally need a residential or business street address for customer identification.

checks.check: New-account address requirements checked before opening
checks.why: Ask which address is for mail and which is required for identity or service. A private mailbox does not guarantee exclusion from credit records.

checks.check: Credit frozen at Equifax, Experian and TransUnion
checks.why: For every adult in the household. Freezes are free.
The phone, pay TV and utility exchange is separate from the three bureaus. Its freeze is free too.

checks.check: Prescreen opt-outs completed through each applicable route
checks.why: Use OptOutPrescreen for participating credit bureaus. A permanent opt-out needs the mailed election form. NCTUE has a separate prescreen opt-out.

checks.check: Caller ID privacy reviewed with the carrier
checks.why: Request outbound caller ID blocking where available. Federal rules include exceptions for emergency services and certain called-party-paid services. Blocking display does not delete carrier records.
checks.source: 47 CFR 64.1601(b), (d), (f), caller ID privacy and exceptions

checks.check: Separate contact number used for optional sign-ups
checks.why: Give your usual number only when needed. Phone numbers can appear in search results. A separate number does not make an account anonymous.
checks.source: Google Search Help, Results about you

checks.check: Relevant Google results reviewed for personal addresses
checks.why: Google accepts personal-information removal requests, subject to its policies. Removing a Search result does not remove the information from the source website.
checks.source: Google Search Help, Results about you

checks.check: Results about you notifications enabled where available
checks.why: Choose email notifications in Results about you. Google can notify you when it finds matching personal information. Coverage and availability vary.
checks.source: Google Search Help, Results about you

checks.check: People-search requests tracked and rechecked monthly
checks.why: Consumer Reports' 2024 study followed 32 volunteers across 13 sites. Every participant still had information listed after four months.
checks.source: Consumer Reports, people-search removal study release, August 8, 2024

checks.check: School directory choices reviewed every school year
checks.why: Read each school's current directory notice and deadline. Submit or renew an opt-out when required, and confirm which information it covers.
checks.source: US Department of Education, directory information

checks.check: School and team contact-sharing choices checked
checks.why: Schools may designate participation in activities and sports as directory information. Check the school's notice. Private clubs set their own policies.

checks.check: No public photos that show the house or school
checks.why: Including location tags on family accounts. A phone photo can store the exact place it was taken, and people you share it with can see it.

checks.check: Street View blur requested and outcome checked
checks.why: Google says an applied Street View blur is permanent. Use its current request and proof-of-address process, then confirm the result.
checks.source: Google Maps Help, Blur Street View Imagery

checks.check: Listing photo removal requested and outcome checked
checks.why: Use each platform's current owner or support route and record its response. A request is not a confirmed removal.
checks.source: Zillow Help, hiding or removing home photos

checks.check: Private mailbox used for deliveries it accepts
checks.why: Confirm acceptance with your mailbox provider. A CMRA receives postal mail for customers. Private-carrier services and delivery details depend on the provider.

checks.check: Your attorney reviews disclosures before the purchase
checks.why: Ask your attorney how filings will show names and addresses. Florida's recording rules generally require grantee names and post-office addresses. Your attorney decides title.
